item: A rollup build the corpus swap killed keeps no hold, so the keyword rollup is rebuilt from the new file instead of staying off until a restart
refs: item 1 exclusive window vs rollup build; R172; R189; 0.5.1 follow-on; PR pending
summary: A restore, a repair or an encryption in place replaces the corpus file under library_generation.swap_window, which refuses every connection made before it. A rollup build holds one session for its whole run and takes no corpus lease, so the swap does not wait for it: reproduced (keyword-lane/swap-midbuild-repro.py), the swap returned in 0.00 s with the build in flight, the build's next statement raised StaleLibraryError and _build_and_swap kept a build-failed hold whose epoch and mention count were read after the swap (the new corpus's), so no wall-branch release rule could fire for a restored corpus of the same size and the keyword rollup stayed off until a restart (live queries meanwhile: latency, never a wrong answer). Now _library_replaced(exc) (the exception or a cause is StaleLibraryError) skips _record_failure; the outcome stays failed, last_decline says library-replaced for the boot row and status, the run of failures stays 0, and the next request rebuilds. Any other error still holds (R172 tests unchanged). LIMITS: a rollup built before the swap and served after it is the separate token/backstop bound (identical-token restore not measured); Windows handle behaviour not measured (Linux sandbox); the persisted refresh raises through the same branch but the persisted store is not exercised by the repro.
